highlights: The native Our Work portfolio contains ten cards: Apollo 1, QDH, Astra, QDB, QDA, joint Draco II/III, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Apex and NASA Valkyrie. Current Apollo 2 is a separate product page; the generic Apollo family is retained.

The 2023 unnumbered Apollo announcement supplies a dated 160 lb, 5 ft 8 in, 55 lb lifting and four-hour-per-pack configuration. Exact aliasing to Apollo 1 and inheritance by Apollo 2 remain unproven; older unsourced price/speed values are withheld.

Apollo 2 offers bipedal/wheeled alternatives and describes expressive status interfaces. Swap-enabled 7x22 operation, opportunity charging and tethering do not establish single-pack endurance or full recharge duration. The 90%+ claim concerns actuator-platform efficiency.

Artemis is the robot-control layer and Fleet Connect the fleet-operation layer, not additional robot hardware. Gemini/Google DeepMind collaborations and configurable safety zones do not establish completed universal autonomy, safe public deployment or whole-robot certification.

Upper-body platforms, dynamic bipeds, the gravity-compensated Scorpio arm and powered Sagittarius/Apex wearables retain their different physical roles. Shared Draco 10-DOF text does not separately certify both named generations, and qualitative spring/force-offload claims are not numerical payload ratings.

The Valkyrie card describes co-founder/team contributions to NASA’s project. NASA Johnson Space Center remains the developer/manufacturer attribution for the separately sourced R5 robot; Apptronik participation is not an Apptronik-built product identity. Historical portfolio cards do not certify present production/support.
